newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Soccer-FAI Cup final doubt over Shelbourne's Morle.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-FAI Cup final doubt over Shelbourne's Morle.

text.p: Shelbourne manager Damien Richardson on Friday said striker Pat Morley was very doubtful for Sunday's Football Association of Ireland (FAI) Cup final against Derry City at Dalymount Park (kick-off 1400 GMT).

"Pat is very doubtful at the moment. His knee is still giving him plenty of trouble and he's receiving extensive treatment each day," Richardson, who led Shelbourne to FAI Cup final glory in 1996, said.
"We put him in against Dundalk in the league last week but he only lasted half the game," he added.

Morley will be sorely missed not least by his striking partner Stephen Geoghegan. The pair built up a good understanding as Shelbourne advanced to a third place finish behind champions Derry City in this season's national league of Ireland premier division.
Geoghegan, 26, finished the season as the premier league's joint top scorer with 16 goals in 33 games while Morley tied for third spot in the scoring charts on 15 goals.
Dessie Baker, 19, a winner of a FA Youths Cup final winners medal with Manchester United in 1995 will probably partner Geoghegan up-front on Sunday.
Baker signed a two year contract with Shelbourne on his return to his native Dublin last summer.
In midfield play-maker Tony Sheridan, Shelbourne have another potential match winner.
Sheridan, 22, does not score that many goals himself but the goals he does score tend to be either very memorable or very significant.
A former first team player with Coventry City in the English professional league, Sheridan scored a brilliant late equaliser against St.Patrick's Athletic to take last year's Cup final to a replay.
He was again on the mark as Shelbourne won the replay.
Shelbourne may have to rely on one moment of individual brilliance or good fortune on Sunday to breach a Derry City defence with the second meanest record in the league.
Derry had lost only four times and had conceded a mere 27 goals when the season came to an end last weekend.

The Northern Ireland side has an impressive record at the other end of the field too with the trio of Peter Hutton, Gary Beckett and Sean Hargan accounting for 36 of the 58 goals Derry City scored during the campaign.
Derry are particularly strong through the middle of the park with two no-nonsense centre-halves in Gavin Dykes and Paul Curran, the strong running Hutton in midfield and the wily Liam Coyle up front.
The hitherto notoriously sceptical and critical Derry City fans have responded well to the current team.
They have returned in their droves to the club's ground, The Brandywell, for home league games and 10,000 Derry City supporters are expected to travel to Dublin for Sunday's game.
TEAMS: SHELBOURNE (probable) - Alan Gough; Pascal
Vaudequin, Greg Costello, Mick Neville, Declan Geoghegan; John O'Rourke, Brian Flood, Tony Sheridan, Mark Rutherford; Stephen Geoghegan, Dessie Baker.
DERRY CITY (probable) - Tony O'Dowd; Declan Boyle, Paul Curran, Gavin Dykes, Tommy Dunne; Sean Hargan, Peter Hutton, Paul Hegarty, James Keddy; Gary Beckett, Liam Coyle.
